facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The financial base is strong but narrow in what it proves. At June 30, 2026 BAYTEX ENERGY CORP. had no drawings on its C$750 million secured revolving credit facilities (maturing June 27, 2030) and one note series, the 7.375% Senior Notes due March 15, 2032, with US$64.1 million (C$91,107 thousand) outstanding, against cash of C$720,337 thousand and company-defined net cash of C$566,286 thousand. Computed liquidity (cash plus undrawn facilities net of letters of credit) was C$1,465,937 thousand. The covenant tests print Total Debt to Bank EBITDA at 0.1 times against a 4.0 times maximum and interest coverage at 9.3 times against a 3.5 times minimum; Bank EBITDA for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 was C$758.9 million. The reading is restricted in four ways. First, all leverage and cover ratios use Bank EBITDA or company-defined net cash, which are company measures pro forma for the sale; the issuer reports no EBITDA, and Bank EBITDA at December 31, 2025 is not in the pack, so the FY2025 ratios are Not supplied. Second, Q2 2026 interest is tiny (net cash interest was income), so cover ratios will keep changing as pre-sale high-interest quarters leave the trailing twelve months. Third, the pre-2026 comparatives mix consolidated, Canada and discontinued bases. Fourth, non-debt claims are material relative to debt: asset retirement obligations of C$546,500 thousand, lease obligations of C$60,256 thousand and a contested tax reassessment, none of which the debt metrics capture. No guarantor, security or covenant text beyond company summaries is verified.

March 31, 2026: undrawn = 750,000 - 0 - 4,400 = 745,600; liquidity = 757,869 + 745,600 = 1,503,469. December 31, 2025: 953,113 + 744,200 (company-stated capacity) = 1,697,313; cross-check 750,000 - 1,400 - 4,400 = 744,200. Inputs E1, E13, E44, E14, E12, E46, E40. - C2 Covenant Total Debt tie-out. Notes principal 91,107 + letters of credit 4,400 = 95,507, which rounds to the printed C$95.5m (E15, E12, E10). - C3 Leverage ratios (x). Total Debt / Bank EBITDA: Q2 2026 95.5 / 758.9 = 0.1258, shown 0.13; Q1 2026 93.9 / 661.0 = 0.1421, shown 0.14. Net cash / Bank EBITDA: Q2 2026 -566.286 / 758.9 = -0.7462, shown -0.75; Q1 2026 -591.151 / 661.0 = -0.8943, shown -0.89. Negative = net cash. Inputs E8, E9, E41, E42, E51, E52b. - C5 Covenant headroom (June 30, 2026). Interest coverage floor: 3.5 x 81.5 = 285.25 (C$m); headroom 758.9 - 285.25 = 473.65 (C$m), 473.65 / 758.9 = 62.4%. facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: BAYTEX ENERGY CORP. is an Alberta-incorporated, listed oil and gas producer whose retained business is entirely in the Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin: heavy oil at Peace River, Peavine and Lloydminster, and light oil in the Viking and the Pembina and Gilby Duvernay (B1, B7, B8, B17). The defining transaction is the sale of the U.S. Eagle Ford assets, completed on December 19, 2025 for net proceeds of US$2.2 billion (C$3.0 billion) (B2, B3). Management states that it then repaid the majority of the credit facilities, redeemed the 8.5% Senior Notes and partially redeemed the 7.375% Senior Notes (B5), leaving one note series of US$64.1 million, an undrawn secured revolver and net cash of C$566,286 thousand at June 30, 2026 (from the financial handoff). For a creditor the mechanism is clear: the sale converted a leveraged, two-country borrower into a debt-light single-basin producer, which removes refinancing and debt-service risk in the near term and moves the credit question to commodity exposure, capital returns and non-debt claims. Three things carry that question. First, revenue is price-taking: realised heavy oil prices track Western Canada Select with a differential and diluent cost (B9, B10, B25), and the legacy oil hedges that cost C$84,146 thousand of realized losses in Q2 2026 have expired, leaving no WTI hedges after Q2 2026 (B11), so cash flow now moves fully with oil prices. Second, management's declared priority is to return cash through buybacks while maintaining the dividend (B4, B20), and buybacks plus dividends exceeded free cash flow in the first half of 2026 (financial handoff; B33), so the cash buffer is discretionary. Third, the pack contains no ownership, control, rating, sponsor or sale-agreement document, so ownership concentration, control rights and the sale's indemnities are Insufficient Information rather than adverse findings. Management's claims (an "industry-leading balance sheet", a net cash position maintained through 2028, a long-term sustaining break-even target) are tagged Management Language and are not adopted.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: The one transaction in the pack is a disposal, not a debt financing. Type: sale of the operated and non-operated Eagle Ford assets, the whole U.S. operating segment (B2). Parties: Baytex as seller; the buyer is not named in any pinned source (Not supplied). Status: completed on December 19, 2025 (B3). Consideration: net proceeds of US$2.2 billion, C$3.0 billion in Canadian dollars after closing adjustments (B3), shown in the results release as an acquisitions and (divestitures) line of (3,006,514) thousand in Q4 2025; post-closing adjustments of C$6.3 million in Q2 2026 and C$18.6 million for the six months are recorded within discontinued operations (S6 page:7). Sponsor: none; Baytex is listed, and the run context names no sponsor. Use of proceeds: management states that Baytex repaid the majority of its credit facilities, redeemed the 8.5% Senior Notes and partially redeemed the 7.375% Senior Notes in Q4 2025 (B5), then resumed share buybacks on December 24, 2025 (S3 page:6). Liquidity effect: cash of C$953,113 thousand at December 31, 2025, against C$1,400 thousand of credit facility drawings and C$95,947 thousand of 7.375% notes (financial handoff). Loss and accounting effects: the 2025 net loss reflected a loss on the Eagle Ford disposition, a deferred tax adjustment related to the transaction structure and a Viking impairment (B40, B41), with management stating no cash-flow impact. Terms not in the pack: purchase agreement, indemnities, retained liabilities and escrow; the Q2 2026 discussion states that Baytex retains liability for matters related to its prior ownership of assets located in the U.S., without amount (S7 page:50). There are no new debt issues in the evidence period: the only debt event after the sale is the repurchase and cancellation of US$5.8 million of 7.375% notes in Q1 2026 at 103.613% of par (S6 page:10), and the revolving facilities were reset between September 30, 2025 and March 31, 2026 to C$750 million maturing June 27, 2030 with no amending document in the pack (financial handoff, gap H5). A second structural transaction is the Gibson infrastructure agreement: Gibson funded Baytex's construction of oil and gas infrastructure under a 15-year take-or-pay agreement, ownership transferred to Gibson in February 2026 at cost, and the agreement was determined to contain a lease, adding lease obligations (B21a, B22a, B23a). Subsequent events after June 30, 2026 in the pack: a dividend declared July 30, 2026, board changes, and buybacks through July 29, 2026 (B28, B38, B42).

It should build the credit view from the financial handoff and these rows: a debt-light, single-basin, price-taking producer whose creditor protection rests on a discretionary cash buffer, with large non-debt claims and no ownership, sale-agreement or debt-document evidence in the pack. Carry forward gaps H1 to H9 and J1 to J8, and the correction that adjusted funds flow on the two perimeters is explained by the discontinued-operations component. Do not treat Insufficient Information rows as adverse findings, and do not adopt Management Language rows. Next evidence action: the annual report exhibits, the sale agreement, the credit agreement and note indenture, and any filing after August 5, 2026.

rows.label: Baytex is now a focused Canadian oil producer after selling its Eagle Ford assets. No sponsor or controlling owner is identified in the pack. It holds strong cash and prioritises buybacks; heavy oil and Duvernay growth drive the plan.
The Eagle Ford sale closed on December 19, 2025 and proceeds were used to repay nearly all debt.
Buybacks and dividends are the stated priority for cash, and they exceeded free cash flow in the first half of 2026.
Output is price-taking heavy oil and Duvernay liquids, and oil hedges against West Texas Intermediate have run off.
Ownership, control and the sale terms are not documented in the pack.
Creditor-adverse actions (priming, uptiering, drop-downs, collateral release)
Revenue durability and price exposure (Analyst Interpretation)
Capital allocation and creditor protection (Analyst Interpretation)

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: BAYTEX ENERGY CORP. is a low-leverage credit with strong near-term liquidity, but its business is fully exposed to oil prices and its cash buffer is one that management can spend. The strongest support is liquidity: C$720,337 thousand of cash and C$745,600 thousand of undrawn committed facilities against C$91,107 thousand (US$64.1 million) of 7.375% notes due March 15, 2032, with Total Debt at 0.13x Bank EBITDA. The weakest point is that free cash flow follows oil prices, the oil hedges have run off, and buybacks plus dividends exceeded free cash flow in the first half of 2026. The outcome depends on whether management keeps net cash as it has said it will, and on what the missing debt documents allow it to distribute.

Liquidity (cash plus undrawn facilities net of letters of credit) was C$1,465,937 thousand. Interest cover on the credit-agreement measure was 9.31x against a 3.5x minimum, and Total Debt was 0.13x Bank EBITDA against a 4.0x maximum. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The issuer has almost no debt after the Eagle Ford sale: C$91,107 thousand of notes principal, undrawn facilities and net cash of C$566,286 thousand, so leverage on the company's own measures is 0.13x and net cash is 0.75x of Bank EBITDA (Documentary Fact; calculated in the financial handoff). Liquidity of C$1,465,937 thousand is about 16.1x the note principal, and no drawn debt principal falls due before 2032 (the notes), while the undrawn revolver commitment matures in 2030 (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the multiple). Covenant headroom is wide: interest cover of 9.31x against 3.5x means Bank EBITDA could fall by about C$473.65 million before breach if the denominator stayed at C$81.5 million (Analyst Interpretation; the denominator is a credit-agreement measure, not cash interest). Operations are strengthening: production of 71,243 boe/d, adjusted funds flow of C$254,433 thousand and free cash flow of C$128,045 thousand in Q2 2026, with 2026 production guidance raised to about 71,000 boe/d (Documentary Fact; the outlook is Management Language). Cash interest is now immaterial: net cash interest was income of C$702 thousand in Q2 2026 (Documentary Fact). Reporting is transparent, with covenants and perimeter disclosed each quarter (Analyst Interpretation).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. The issuer is a price-taker: heavy oil is 65% of production, realised heavy prices follow Western Canada Select less a differential that widened to US$14.62 per barrel from US$10.20, and no WTI hedges remain after Q2 2026 (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the margin mechanism). It has one basin and one country after the sale, so egress, royalty and regulatory exposure are concentrated (Analyst Interpretation). Cash returns are discretionary and exceeded free cash flow in the first half of 2026, so net cash is a policy choice that can be reversed (Documentary Fact on the amounts, Analyst Interpretation on the reading). Non-debt claims of C$606,756 thousand for asset retirement and leases, plus the contested tax reassessment, are not reflected in debt ratios (Documentary Fact; sum calculated here). The covenant and leverage measures are company-defined, the issuer reports no EBITDA, and the debt documents that would show guarantors, security, baskets and call terms are not in the pack (Insufficient Information on the terms: the missing datapoint is the credit agreement and note indenture, and it matters because restricted-payment limits decide how much of the buffer is protected). Ownership and control are not documented, and the sale agreement and its indemnities are not in the pack (Insufficient Information; absence is not an adverse conclusion).

Ownership, the sale terms and the debt agreements are not documented in the pack.

Low financial risk and strong liquidity today; moderate to elevated business risk from price exposure, expired hedges and single-basin concentration; creditor protection uncertain because cash returns are discretionary and the debt documents are not in the pack.

BAYTEX ENERGY CORP. is a debt-light, price-taking Canadian oil producer whose credit quality today rests on a discretionary cash buffer rather than on contractual protections that the pack can verify.

As-of date 2026-11-05; evidence cutoff 2026-11-05. Pathway: credit snapshot. Reporting currency per run context: CAD (all pinned financial statements are in thousands of Canadian dollars, with US$ amounts labelled). Current period per context: Q2 2026 (quarter ended June 30, 2026); prior period: FY2025.

Question: can the pinned source set support the four requested downstream consumers (CP-1 financial data, CP-1A business and transaction context, CP-2 fundamental credit synthesis, CP-5 evidence trace validation), and what remains blocked? This module gives no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no investment opinion, and it does not normalize, reconcile or calculate figures. No upstream handoff exists for this module (it is first in the run).

The run context names no borrower, no parent, no guarantors, no ratings, no market data, no deal terms and no legal documents ("legal_documents": "none"). Blank context values are treated as not supplied, not as zero.

### Financial base view

The financial base is strong but narrow in what it proves. At June 30, 2026 BAYTEX ENERGY CORP. had no drawings on its C$750 million secured revolving credit facilities (maturing June 27, 2030) and one note series, the 7.375% Senior Notes due March 15, 2032, with US$64.1 million (C$91,107 thousand) outstanding, against cash of C$720,337 thousand and company-defined net cash of C$566,286 thousand. Computed liquidity (cash plus undrawn facilities net of letters of credit) was C$1,465,937 thousand. The covenant tests print Total Debt to Bank EBITDA at 0.1 times against a 4.0 times maximum and interest coverage at 9.3 times against a 3.5 times minimum; Bank EBITDA for the twelve months to June 30, 2026 was C$758.9 million. The reading is restricted in four ways. First, all leverage and cover ratios use Bank EBITDA or company-defined net cash, which are company measures pro forma for the sale; the issuer reports no EBITDA, and Bank EBITDA at December 31, 2025 is not in the pack, so the FY2025 ratios are Not supplied. Second, Q2 2026 interest is tiny (net cash interest was income), so cover ratios will keep changing as pre-sale high-interest quarters leave the trailing twelve months. Third, the pre-2026 comparatives mix consolidated, Canada and discontinued bases. Fourth, non-debt claims are material relative to debt: asset retirement obligations of C$546,500 thousand, lease obligations of C$60,256 thousand and a contested tax reassessment, none of which the debt metrics capture. No guarantor, security or covenant text beyond company summaries is verified.

## Calculations
All inputs are quoted in the evidence register (C$k unless stated). Python-checked.

- **C1 Liquidity (cash plus undrawn facilities net of letters of credit).** June 30, 2026: undrawn = 750,000 - 0 - 4,400 = 745,600; liquidity = 720,337 + 745,600 = 1,465,937. March 31, 2026: undrawn = 750,000 - 0 - 4,400 = 745,600; liquidity = 757,869 + 745,600 = 1,503,469. December 31, 2025: 953,113 + 744,200 (company-stated capacity) = 1,697,313; cross-check 750,000 - 1,400 - 4,400 = 744,200. Inputs E1, E13, E44, E14, E12, E46, E40.
- **C2 Covenant Total Debt tie-out.** Notes principal 91,107 + letters of credit 4,400 = 95,507, which rounds to the printed C$95.5m (E15, E12, E10).

- **C3 Leverage ratios (x).** Total Debt / Bank EBITDA: Q2 2026 95.5 / 758.9 = 0.1258, shown 0.13; Q1 2026 93.9 / 661.0 = 0.1421, shown 0.14. Net cash / Bank EBITDA: Q2 2026 -566.286 / 758.9 = -0.7462, shown -0.75; Q1 2026 -591.151 / 661.0 = -0.8943, shown -0.89. Negative = net cash. Inputs E10, E43b, E8, E41, E17, E26.

- **C4 Interest cover (x).** Q2 2026 758.9 / 81.5 = 9.3117, shown 9.31; Q1 2026 661.0 / 119.4 = 5.5360, shown 5.54. Q3 2025 is taken as printed (10.5) because Bank EBITDA is rounded ($1.9 billion / $183.0m = 10.38 would be false precision). Inputs E8, E9, E41, E42, E51, E52b.

- **C5 Covenant headroom (June 30, 2026).** Interest coverage floor: 3.5 x 81.5 = 285.25 (C$m); headroom 758.9 - 285.25 = 473.65 (C$m), 473.65 / 758.9 = 62.4%. Total Debt cap: 4.0 x 758.9 = 3,035.6 (C$m) versus 95.5. Senior secured cap: 3.5 x 758.9 = 2,656.15 (C$m) versus 4.4. The interest-coverage figure holds the denominator fixed and is an arithmetic headroom, not a forecast.

- **C7 Net cash change.** 765,785 - 566,286 = 199,499 decline in company-defined net cash from December 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026. The company's own explanation is shareholder returns of 342.9 offset by free cash flow of 129.8 (C$m, E64, E64a); the two are not reconciled here because net cash includes working-capital movements.

- **C8 Quarter-end carrying lines.** Q1 2026 lease obligations 9,439 + 48,783 = 58,222; asset retirement obligations 17,165 + 514,613 = 531,778 (S4 page:1). Q1 2026 net loss from continuing operations check: -67,326 - 12,353 = -79,679 (S4 pages 1 and 2), which agrees with the printed -79,679.

- **C9 Reference: trailing twelve-month adjusted funds flow, continuing basis (cross-check only, not a leverage input).** Q3 2025 151,846 + Q4 2025 116,214 + Q1 2026 152,211 + Q2 2026 254,433 = 674,704 (E31, E30, E18). Notes principal 91,107 / 674,704 = 0.135 times. Adjusted funds flow is after cash interest and realized hedging, so it is not EBITDA; the Q3 and Q4 2025 inputs are the March 2026 "Canada" presentation. Implied reduction in the 7.375% notes from US$575.0m at September 30, 2025 to US$70.0m at December 31, 2025 is 505.0 (US$m), from S2 page:10 and S6 page:10; redemption dates and prices are Not supplied.

## Findings
### Reader summary

It holds strong cash and prioritises buybacks; heavy oil and Duvernay growth drive the plan. | Medium | The annual information form, ownership detail and sale documents are not in the pack, so ownership, asset quality and sale terms rest on press releases and notes. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

### Business and transaction view

BAYTEX ENERGY CORP. is an Alberta-incorporated, listed oil and gas producer whose retained business is entirely in the Western Canadian Sedimentary Basin: heavy oil at Peace River, Peavine and Lloydminster, and light oil in the Viking and the Pembina and Gilby Duvernay (B1, B7, B8, B17). The defining transaction is the sale of the U.S. Eagle Ford assets, completed on December 19, 2025 for net proceeds of US$2.2 billion (C$3.0 billion) (B2, B3). Management states that it then repaid the majority of the credit facilities, redeemed the 8.5% Senior Notes and partially redeemed the 7.375% Senior Notes (B5), leaving one note series of US$64.1 million, an undrawn secured revolver and net cash of C$566,286 thousand at June 30, 2026 (from the financial handoff). For a creditor the mechanism is clear: the sale converted a leveraged, two-country borrower into a debt-light single-basin producer, which removes refinancing and debt-service risk in the near term and moves the credit question to commodity exposure, capital returns and non-debt claims. Three things carry that question. First, revenue is price-taking: realised heavy oil prices track Western Canada Select with a differential and diluent cost (B9, B10, B25), and the legacy oil hedges that cost C$84,146 thousand of realized losses in Q2 2026 have expired, leaving no WTI hedges after Q2 2026 (B11), so cash flow now moves fully with oil prices. Second, management's declared priority is to return cash through buybacks while maintaining the dividend (B4, B20), and buybacks plus dividends exceeded free cash flow in the first half of 2026 (financial handoff; B33), so the cash buffer is discretionary. Third, the pack contains no ownership, control, rating, sponsor or sale-agreement document, so ownership concentration, control rights and the sale's indemnities are Insufficient Information rather than adverse findings. Management's claims (an "industry-leading balance sheet", a net cash position maintained through 2028, a long-term sustaining break-even target) are tagged Management Language and are not adopted.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The one transaction in the pack is a disposal, not a debt financing. Type: sale of the operated and non-operated Eagle Ford assets, the whole U.S. operating segment (B2). Parties: Baytex as seller; the buyer is not named in any pinned source (Not supplied). Status: completed on December 19, 2025 (B3). Consideration: net proceeds of US$2.2 billion, C$3.0 billion in Canadian dollars after closing adjustments (B3), shown in the results release as an acquisitions and (divestitures) line of (3,006,514) thousand in Q4 2025; post-closing adjustments of C$6.3 million in Q2 2026 and C$18.6 million for the six months are recorded within discontinued operations (S6 page:7). Sponsor: none; Baytex is listed, and the run context names no sponsor. Use of proceeds: management states that Baytex repaid the majority of its credit facilities, redeemed the 8.5% Senior Notes and partially redeemed the 7.375% Senior Notes in Q4 2025 (B5), then resumed share buybacks on December 24, 2025 (S3 page:6). Liquidity effect: cash of C$953,113 thousand at December 31, 2025, against C$1,400 thousand of credit facility drawings and C$95,947 thousand of 7.375% notes (financial handoff). Loss and accounting effects: the 2025 net loss reflected a loss on the Eagle Ford disposition, a deferred tax adjustment related to the transaction structure and a Viking impairment (B40, B41), with management stating no cash-flow impact. Terms not in the pack: purchase agreement, indemnities, retained liabilities and escrow; the Q2 2026 discussion states that Baytex retains liability for matters related to its prior ownership of assets located in the U.S., without amount (S7 page:50). There are no new debt issues in the evidence period: the only debt event after the sale is the repurchase and cancellation of US$5.8 million of 7.375% notes in Q1 2026 at 103.613% of par (S6 page:10), and the revolving facilities were reset between September 30, 2025 and March 31, 2026 to C$750 million maturing June 27, 2030 with no amending document in the pack (financial handoff, gap H5). A second structural transaction is the Gibson infrastructure agreement: Gibson funded Baytex's construction of oil and gas infrastructure under a 15-year take-or-pay agreement, ownership transferred to Gibson in February 2026 at cost, and the agreement was determined to contain a lease, adding lease obligations (B21a, B22a, B23a). Subsequent events after June 30, 2026 in the pack: a dividend declared July 30, 2026, board changes, and buybacks through July 29, 2026 (B28, B38, B42).

spans.text: ## Request

This is the fundamental credit synthesis for BAYTEX ENERGY CORP. (issuer id bte), as of 2026-11-05 with an evidence cutoff of 2026-11-05. The pathway is credit snapshot, in Canadian dollars. It synthesises the accepted financial (CP-1) and business and transaction (CP-1A) handoffs only, and reads no source text.
## Sources
### Issuer sources behind the upstream handoffs
This module quotes no source text; the sources below are those on which the upstream handoffs rest, listed with their exact names and sha256.
| Alias | Exact source name | sha256 |
Run context: /workspace/secdata/data/2026-11-05/contexts/1279495-baytex-energy-corp-bte.json, sha256 a4beb54d12cde8b01d2e19e329c06ce5b476e74c9a66d64a29ea9c069505e245.
### Supplied handoffs
| Module | sha256 | Basis name used below |
| CP-0 | 68599e57819209c904b32c5e729b1780b103c65bf8c26f89178fef7d84c1f1ef | Source readiness (gaps G1 to G10) |

| CP-1 | aa3453dc0f8d425d3b66d145888845acf28f20d2c2a05f86208a8401329bec01 | Financial handoff: tables "Financials and credit metrics", "Debt register", "Claims outside debt", "Liquidity", "Covenants", calculations C1 to C9, gaps H1 to H9 |

| CP-1A | 6499170f9e77a8dc035850243b0c8922ee81f9c50f3b659fe2b401b3a1bba1da | Business handoff: tables "Company and operating model", "Governance and capital allocation", "Credit translations", gaps J1 to J8 |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Baytex has very little debt, strong liquidity and wide covenant headroom today. Its credit quality rests on a cash buffer that management can spend and on oil prices it does not control. | Medium | Debt agreements, ownership and sale documents are missing, and the company reports no EBITDA, so leverage rests on company-defined measures. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt service risk is minimal at current balances: one small note series, an undrawn revolver and large cash. | Near-term default and refinancing risk are low; the notes fall due in 2032 and the revolver in 2030. | High |
| Free cash flow swings with oil prices and the oil hedges have expired. | Cash generation and the cash buffer move with prices, with no hedge cushion in the second half of 2026. | Medium |

| Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in the first half of 2026, and management prioritises buybacks. | Net cash is discretionary and can fall without any default trigger, so low leverage today does not fix future leverage. | High |

| Asset retirement obligations, leases and a contested tax reassessment sit outside the debt metrics. | Total claims on cash are much larger than the note principal, and the covenant debt definition excludes the first two. | Medium |

| Ownership, the sale terms and the debt agreements are not documented in the pack. | Protections against distributions or priming cannot be tested; the gap limits confidence and is not an adverse finding. | Medium |
### Credit view

BAYTEX ENERGY CORP. is a low-leverage credit with strong near-term liquidity, but its business is fully exposed to oil prices and its cash buffer is one that management can spend. The strongest support is liquidity: C$720,337 thousand of cash and C$745,600 thousand of undrawn committed facilities against C$91,107 thousand (US$64.1 million) of 7.375% notes due March 15, 2032, with Total Debt at 0.13x Bank EBITDA. The weakest point is that free cash flow follows oil prices, the oil hedges have run off, and buybacks plus dividends exceeded free cash flow in the first half of 2026. The outcome depends on whether management keeps net cash as it has said it will, and on what the missing debt documents allow it to distribute.
### Key findings

First, the issuer's debt burden is small enough that debt service is not a near-term concern. After the Eagle Ford sale it had no drawings on its C$750 million secured revolving credit facilities, which mature June 27, 2030, and C$91,107 thousand of notes, against cash of C$720,337 thousand and company-defined net cash of C$566,286 thousand at June 30, 2026. Liquidity (cash plus undrawn facilities net of letters of credit) was C$1,465,937 thousand. Interest cover on the credit-agreement measure was 9.31x against a 3.5x minimum, and Total Debt was 0.13x Bank EBITDA against a 4.0x maximum. [Financial handoff; Analyst Interpretation on the reading, Documentary Fact on the figures.]

Second, the credit question has moved from the debt stack to the cash buffer. Management states that buybacks are the priority and targets 15% annual total shareholder return, and in the six months to June 30, 2026 shareholder returns of C$342.9 million exceeded free cash flow of C$129.8 million. Company-defined net cash fell from C$765,785 thousand to C$566,286 thousand over the same period. Because the stated three-year plan is to maintain net cash, but the restricted-payment baskets in the debt documents are not in the pack, creditors cannot tell how much of the buffer is contractually protected. [Financial and business handoffs; Documentary Fact for the amounts, Management Language for the plan, Analyst Interpretation for the reading.]

Third, cash generation is price-driven and no longer hedged. Free cash flow was C$1,705 thousand in Q1 2026 when WTI averaged US$71.93 per barrel and C$128,045 thousand in Q2 2026 when it averaged US$92.79, and the issuer states that it has no WTI hedges after Q2 2026. The legacy hedges cost C$84,146 thousand of realized derivative losses in Q2 2026. A price fall would therefore pass straight through to adjusted funds flow, which was C$254,433 thousand in Q2 2026. [Analyst Interpretation on the sensitivity, Documentary Fact on the figures.]

Fourth, claims outside the debt metrics are large. Asset retirement obligations were C$546,500 thousand and lease obligations C$60,256 thousand at June 30, 2026, both excluded from the covenant debt definition, and the Canada Revenue Agency asserts C$244.8 million of tax, C$244.2 million of late-payment interest and a C$4.1 million penalty on a reassessment the issuer contests and for which it purchased C$272.5 million of insurance coverage. These claims need cash that low debt ratios do not show. [Financial and business handoffs; Documentary Fact.]

Fifth, the evidence base limits how far the favourable picture can be pushed. The issuer reports no EBITDA, Bank EBITDA is a company-defined measure pro forma for the sale, the FY2025 ratios are Not supplied, and comparatives before 2026 mix reporting bases. Ownership, the sale agreement and the debt documents are absent, which is Insufficient Information, not an adverse finding. [Source readiness, financial and business handoffs.]
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The issuer has almost no debt after the Eagle Ford sale: C$91,107 thousand of notes principal, undrawn facilities and net cash of C$566,286 thousand, so leverage on the company's own measures is 0.13x and net cash is 0.75x of Bank EBITDA (Documentary Fact; calculated in the financial handoff). Liquidity of C$1,465,937 thousand is about 16.1x the note principal, and no drawn debt principal falls due before 2032 (the notes), while the undrawn revolver commitment matures in 2030 (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the multiple). Covenant headroom is wide: interest cover of 9.31x against 3.5x means Bank EBITDA could fall by about C$473.65 million before breach if the denominator stayed at C$81.5 million (Analyst Interpretation; the denominator is a credit-agreement measure, not cash interest). Operations are strengthening: production of 71,243 boe/d, adjusted funds flow of C$254,433 thousand and free cash flow of C$128,045 thousand in Q2 2026, with 2026 production guidance raised to about 71,000 boe/d (Documentary Fact; the outlook is Management Language). Cash interest is now immaterial: net cash interest was income of C$702 thousand in Q2 2026 (Documentary Fact). Reporting is transparent, with covenants and perimeter disclosed each quarter (Analyst Interpretation).

Weaknesses. The issuer is a price-taker: heavy oil is 65% of production, realised heavy prices follow Western Canada Select less a differential that widened to US$14.62 per barrel from US$10.20, and no WTI hedges remain after Q2 2026 (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation on the margin mechanism). It has one basin and one country after the sale, so egress, royalty and regulatory exposure are concentrated (Analyst Interpretation). Cash returns are discretionary and exceeded free cash flow in the first half of 2026, so net cash is a policy choice that can be reversed (Documentary Fact on the amounts, Analyst Interpretation on the reading). Non-debt claims of C$606,756 thousand for asset retirement and leases, plus the contested tax reassessment, are not reflected in debt ratios (Documentary Fact; sum calculated here). The covenant and leverage measures are company-defined, the issuer reports no EBITDA, and the debt documents that would show guarantors, security, baskets and call terms are not in the pack (Insufficient Information on the terms: the missing datapoint is the credit agreement and note indenture, and it matters because restricted-payment limits decide how much of the buffer is protected). Ownership and control are not documented, and the sale agreement and its indemnities are not in the pack (Insufficient Information; absence is not an adverse conclusion).
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Low financial risk and strong liquidity today; moderate to elevated business risk from price exposure, expired hedges and single-basin concentration; creditor protection uncertain because cash returns are discretionary and the debt documents are not in the pack. | Analyst Interpretation | Medium (below High because the business handoff records High-severity gaps J1 to J3 and a READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS judgment of this module) | Financial handoff: Financials and credit metrics, Liquidity, Covenants; business handoff: Company and operating model, Governance and capital allocation, Credit translations |
### Thesis
| Thesis | Category | Basis |

| BAYTEX ENERGY CORP. is a debt-light, price-taking Canadian oil producer whose credit quality today rests on a discretionary cash buffer rather than on contractual protections that the pack can verify. | Analyst Interpretation | Financial handoff: Debt register, Liquidity; business handoff: Governance and capital allocation |
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Oil price and differential exposure | Sales are benchmark-linked, the hedge book that muted 2025 volatility has expired, royalties rise with price and the Western Canada Select differential widened | Free cash flow and net cash fall quickly in a price decline; covenant ratios stay wide but liquidity is the first thing to erode | Material | Business handoff: Credit translations (revenue durability, margin); financial handoff: Financials and credit metrics |

| Discretionary distributions | Buybacks and dividends are the stated priority and exceeded free cash flow in the first half of 2026; restricted-payment baskets are not in the pack | Net cash can fall without a covenant breach, so leverage can rise from near zero; protection depends on documents not seen | Material | Business handoff: Governance and capital allocation; financial handoff: Covenants, gap H2 |

| Non-debt claims on cash | Asset retirement obligations of C$546,500 thousand and leases of C$60,256 thousand are outside covenant Total Debt; the CRA reassessment asserts C$493.1 million in total | Fixed cash calls and a contingent tax outcome compete with debt service for the same cash flow | Material | Financial handoff: Claims outside debt; business handoff: Credit translations |

| Single-basin concentration | All production is in Western Canada after the sale, with heavy oil 65% of volume | Egress, royalty and regulatory exposure are concentrated; growth capital is directed to the same basin | Material | Business handoff: Company and operating model |

| Information gaps on protections | No credit agreement, indenture, ownership or sale documents in the pack | Guarantor, security and anti-priming protections cannot be tested; weakens confidence, not a finding of weakness | Material | Source readiness gaps G1 to G3; business handoff gaps J1 to J3 |

| Refinancing and maturity | Revolver matures June 27, 2030; notes mature March 15, 2032 and are callable from March 15, 2027 | No near-term maturity; the undrawn revolver commitment must be renewed by 2030 for liquidity to persist | Minor | Financial handoff: Debt register |
| Comparability of history | Eagle Ford sale changed the perimeter; pre-2026 columns mix bases | Trend and cover comparisons across the sale date can mislead | Minor | Financial handoff: gap H4 |
## Calculations
All inputs are accepted figures of the financial and business handoffs.

- **C1 Non-debt claims.** Asset retirement obligations C$546,500 thousand + lease obligations C$60,256 thousand = C$606,756 thousand (June 30, 2026). Against cash of C$720,337 thousand this is 0.8423 times (84.2%); against notes principal of C$91,107 thousand it is 6.66 times.

- **C2 CRA asserted amounts.** C$244.8 million tax + C$244.2 million late-payment interest + C$4.1 million penalty = C$493.1 million, as asserted in the CRA statement of account; whether any amount is recognised is not stated.
- **C3 Liquidity cover of the notes.** Liquidity C$1,465,937 thousand / notes principal C$91,107 thousand = 16.09x; cash alone C$720,337 thousand / C$91,107 thousand = 7.91x.

- **C4 Distributions versus free cash flow, six months to June 30, 2026.** Share repurchase consideration C$310.1 million + dividends declared C$32.750 million = C$342.85 million, which agrees with the printed C$342.9 million; free cash flow C$129.75 million (printed C$129.8 million); excess = C$213.10 million. This is the same calculation as in the business handoff, repeated for the credit view.

- **C5 Covenant headroom (from the financial handoff).** Interest-cover floor 3.5 x C$81.5 million = C$285.25 million; headroom C$758.9 million - C$285.25 million = C$473.65 million (62.4%). The denominator is held fixed; this is not a forecast.
## Gaps
| ID | Severity | Gap | Why it matters and what it affects | Action |

| K1 | High | Debt agreements (credit agreement with amendments and note indenture) are not in the pack; guarantors, security, restricted-payment baskets, call prices and change-of-control terms are Not supplied | Decides how much of the cash buffer is protected from distributions and priming; limits the risk table and assessment confidence | Add the debt documents |

| K2 | High | The issuer reports no EBITDA; Bank EBITDA is company-defined and pro forma for the sale, with its build-up and the December 31, 2025 value Not supplied | All leverage and cover ratios rest on it; FY2025 ratios are Not supplied | Obtain the credit agreement definitions and the covenant compliance certificate |

| K3 | High | Ownership, control rights and the Eagle Ford sale agreement (buyer, indemnities, retained liabilities and their amount) are Not supplied | Governance and creditor-control conclusions and possible contingent liabilities cannot be assessed | Add the annual information form and sale agreement |

| K4 | Medium | The audited FY2025 statements and notes are not in the pack: year-end covenant table, annual interest paid, any provision for the CRA matter, pensions, factoring and supply-chain finance searches | FY2025 column and completeness of claims outside debt | Add the annual report exhibits |

| K5 | Medium | The pack ends with the Q2 2026 documents (latest event July 30, 2026); the as-of date is November 5, 2026 | Anything filed or happening later, including the third quarter 2026 results if published, is not reflected | Check for later filings before the cutoff |
| K6 | Medium | Restated and unrestated 2025 comparatives mix consolidated, Canada and discontinued bases | Trends across the sale date | Label basis; prefer revised comparatives |

| K7 | Low | No ratings, quotes or market data in the run context; management claims such as an "industry-leading balance sheet" cannot be tested | Strengths are stated on absolute measures only | Add rating and market inputs if the committee needs them |
### Readiness and upstream corrections

This module is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS: its inputs were accepted and its sources are sufficient for a synthesis with bounded gaps. Upstream corrections carried: the financial handoff corrected a sentence of the readiness handoff about Baytex Energy USA, Inc. (it was a borrower under its own facility at September 30, 2025); the business handoff showed that the two year-to-date 2026 adjusted funds flow figures, C$405,558 thousand consolidated and C$406,644 thousand for Canada, differ by the (1,086) thousand discontinued component printed in the Q2 2026 release, so the earlier "not reconciled" notes are superseded. No upstream figure used here was found to be wrong.
## Next module

Proceed to CP-5 (evidence trace validator). It should confirm that each claim above rests on a financial or business handoff row, that Management Language rows (the net cash outlook, break-even targets, "industry-leading balance sheet") are not stated as facts, that Insufficient Information rows (debt documents, ownership, sale agreement) are not cited as support, and that figures match across the three upstream modules. Carry forward gaps K1 to K7. Next evidence action: the debt documents, the annual report exhibits, the sale agreement and any filing after August 5, 2026.
